clue.text: Bay, or lake in a bay

indicators.note: the lake letter is set in among the letters of 'a bay', which wrap around it

parts.note: a cove is a small bay
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A geography question: is that body of water a bay, or a lake sitting in a bay?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside A + COVE, just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess in a wall, and a bay is likewise a recessed part of a room or building.

clue.text: A security device plugged by Conservative flier

indicators.note: something plugged has a stopper pushed into it, so the device's letters take the party letter inside

parts.note: a lock is a device that secures a door
C is the usual abbreviation for Conservative, the UK political party

explanation.surface: A political pilot fits a lock to something, or a Tory airman is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugged by' puts C inside LOCK, after the L. John Alcock flew the first non-stop transatlantic flight in 1919 with Arthur Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Alcock was a pioneering aviator, so he is a famous flier.

clue.text: Finish in French bars, in which aliens may appear

parts.note: a close is an end or conclusion
the French word for in is en
counters are the bars in shops or pubs over which goods or drinks are served

explanation.surface: Ending a night out in Parisian bars, where strange visitors might turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Spielberg's 1977 film about contact with extraterrestrials.
explanation.definitionFit: Close Encounters of the Third Kind is the film about meeting extraterrestrials, and the phrase names any such meeting.

clue.text: See a crook punching really scrupulous men? This gets one's blood pressure up

definitions.text: This gets one's blood pressure up

parts.note: V is the abbreviation of Latin vide, meaning see, used in references

indicators.note: a fist punching something goes into it, so the crook's letters drive into the middle of the other word pair

parts.note: so, as in 'so good', means really
strict means scrupulous, exacting
a con is a swindler or crook (short for con man)
OR (other ranks) is the crossword abbreviation for ordinary soldiers, men

explanation.surface: A villain assaulting principled men, and a reader's blood pressure rising at the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punching' means the crook lands in the middle of 'really scrupulous', not before or after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vasoconstrictor narrows blood vessels, a narrowing that raises blood pressure.

clue.text: Cutting Republican Party decorations shows some craft

indicators.note: cutting a letter means removing it, so the party letter is taken out of the decorations

parts.note: streamers are paper ribbons hung up at parties

explanation.surface: Someone slashing a political party's bunting shows a certain skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' removes R from STREAMERS. 'craft' looks like skill but means vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamers are steamships, and craft is a plural word for boats or vessels.

clue.text: Informed about male composer turning up part in comedy of manners

indicators.note: the informing word goes about, around, the male pronoun

parts.note: told means informed
he is the male pronoun
J. S. Bach is the German composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters for part are read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: A theatre note: told about a male composer who turned up with a part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the enclosure; 'turning up' reverses the part, as this is a down clue. The Old Bachelor is William Congreve's first play (1693).
explanation.definitionFit: Congreve's The Old Bachelor is a Restoration play, an example of the comedy of manners genre.

clue.text: Spreading foreign aid etc., so time to take responsibility

indicators.note: spreading the letters around scatters them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Distributing overseas aid and the like is a sign it is time to grow up and be accountable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreading' rearranges FOREIGNAIDETCSO.
explanation.definitionFit: The age of discretion is the age at which a person is legally judged able to make their own decisions.

clue.text: Cutting off partner no longer sending emails, say

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
sending emails is one example of communicating

explanation.surface: Cutting an ex out of your life, so that you no longer send emails.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs a break-up with going silent, but the answer is the church's formal expulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To excommunicate is to expel from the church, cutting someone off from the community.

clue.text: Imagines schools must keep distinguishing feature

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the schools word holds the feature

parts.note: sects are schools of thought or religious groups
USP is a unique selling point, a product's distinguishing feature

explanation.surface: Someone fancies that schools need to preserve whatever makes them distinctive.
explanation.walkthrough: USP, short for unique selling point, is marketing jargon for what sets a product apart; 'must keep' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect is to believe or suppose something without proof, which is to imagine it.

clue.text: Travels with Parisian relatives around mostly awful country

indicators.note: the relatives word goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: pères is French for fathers, relatives in Paris

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for awful is used

parts.note: grim means awful
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A trip taken with French family round a mostly dreadful land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the word for awful; 'around' has the French fathers enclose everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Peregrinations are long wanderings or journeys, a literary word for travels.

clue.text: Vexed about soldiers breaking barriers for citations

parts.note: cross means annoyed, vexed
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the soldiers break into the barriers, splitting them open

parts.note: fences are barriers
RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army soldiers

explanation.surface: Annoyed about troops breaking through fences, someone looks for quotations.
explanation.walkthrough: RE does double duty in different senses: 'about' (as in business letters) and the Royal Engineers. 'breaking' splits the barriers after their second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-references are notes directing a reader to another place in a text, a kind of citation.

clue.text: Throwing hammer, feel Czech gets hint about motivation

indicators.note: throwing the letters tosses them about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Czech hammer thrower's feelings give a clue to what drives him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing' rearranges HAMMERFEELCZECH. The answer is French for 'look for the woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase suggests a woman lies behind a man's actions, a hint at his motive.

clue.text: Sillier, injured Americans may end up here

definitions.meaning: the comparative of inane, meaning more foolish

definitions.text: injured Americans may end up here
definitions.meaning: read as three words, the answer is '...', an emergency room in an American hospital

explanation.surface: Foolishness of the kind that lands Americans in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer IN AN ER: ER is the American term for a hospital emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, so the comparative form means sillier.

clue.text: Resident of the UK stores what Spanish fuel?

indicators.note: storing something means holding it inside, so the resident word holds the Spanish word

parts.note: a Brit is a British person
qué is Spanish for what

explanation.surface: A Briton keeps something, and a puzzled question about what Spanish fuel might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' signals the enclosure; the question mark flags that 'what Spanish' is a word in Spanish, not a query.
explanation.definitionFit: A briquet, or briquette, is a block of compressed coal dust or charcoal burned as fuel.

clue.text: A top copper or an offender?

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the UK police detective branch, so stands for copper
the head is the top person, the one in charge

explanation.surface: Is that person the senior police officer or a criminal?
explanation.walkthrough: 'top copper' reads as a head of CID, the senior UK detective; 'or' links it to the definition. The offender is a habitual user of acid, the drug LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is slang for the drug LSD, and its regular users break drug laws.

clue.text: Princess in opera, but not a princess in opera

indicators.note: not a means the letter A is left out of the opera princess's name

parts.note: Aida is the Ethiopian princess in Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about two royal heroines of the operatic stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan; remove A from Verdi's AIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Ida is the title heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.

clue.text: Reason against admitting defeat for one in the soup

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the reason word takes the defeat inside

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
a rout is a heavy defeat

explanation.surface: An argument against conceding defeat for someone who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' signals the enclosure. 'In the soup' looks like trouble, but here means literally floating in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a cube of fried bread floated in soup.

clue.text: A bit of racy clickbait is going around

indicators.note: a bit of the words means just a run of their letters is taken from them

explanation.surface: Some saucy online clickbait is doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of' picks the run spanning raCY CLICkbait.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclic means occurring in cycles, coming round again and again.

clue.text: Proper recession grips financial district

indicators.note: the recession word grips, holds within it, the district's letters

parts.note: a dent is a hollow, a recession in a surface
EC is the postcode of the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: A genuine economic downturn takes hold of the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks economic but means a recess or hollow; EC is the City of London postcode. 'grips' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means proper, respectable or appropriate.

clue.text: Did wrong backing main idea by new, wicked scamp

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for did wrong is read in reverse

parts.note: sinned means did wrong
a theme is a main idea
wicked is slang for excellent, as is ace

explanation.surface: A rascal who sinned by supporting some new and evil scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SINNED into DENNIS. Dennis the Menace is a naughty boy from the British comic The Beano.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis the Menace is the famous comic-strip troublemaker, the archetypal mischievous boy.

clue.text: Criminal perceives loot — it gets kind of charge

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook spots the haul, and that gets him charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges PERCEIVESLOOTIT. 'charge' looks legal but is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Electropositive describes an element or electrode carrying, or tending to give, a positive electrical charge.

clue.text: Chagrin of one gaining stone squeezing into clothing

indicators.note: the pair of pieces squeeze into the clothing, which encloses them

parts.note: dress means clothing

indicators.note: one gaining something has it added on, so the stone letters follow

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: The embarrassment of someone who put on weight and is squeezing into their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' adds the stone after the one; 'squeezing into' puts that pair just after the first letter of the clothing. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or anguish, close to distress in meaning.

clue.text: One may be black or white in dark time, we hear

definitions.text: One may be black or white

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: Something is black or white in the dark, we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K makes the chess piece sound like NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is a chess piece, and each player has pieces of black or white.
